meta.edge_rule: commenter -> parent-comment author (reply) or -> post author (top-level); self-loops dropped; weight = interaction count; mentions not available in the archive

variants.no_autonomy: main minus all activity by agents flagged in the autonomy audit
variants.merged: union of pinned revision and archive head, deduplicated by id (recovers the posts most top-level comments point to)

reference_comparison.cause: agents table of the pinned revision ee98f6c8, identical to the earlier run
10,000 capped memes + 286 skill + 6 behavioral; the earlier run also scanned posts dated 2026-02-21..24
silhouette rises almost monotonically over k=3..8 (0.906 to 0.916); the maximum moved from k=6 to k=8 by 0.0025, within k-means initialisation noise; at k=6 the rerun silhouette is 0.9133
xmin equals the smallest cascade kept by the 10,000 cap (94 adopters here); the cap boundary shifts with the corpus (the earlier run also scanned posts dated 2026-02-21..24)

reference_comparison.quantity: Cox HR (earlier-run procedure, top-100 capped cascades, static exposure)
reference_comparison.cause: the top-100 cascade membership differs (corpus includes only in-window posts; size ties broken by seed time instead of dict insertion order); the static, asymmetric exposure that drives HR < 1 is unchanged
the earlier run counted every post in the revision, including posts created 2026-02-21..24 after the window; without the window filter the count is 60045 (exact match)

sec_res_structure.silhouette_interpretation: the silhouette is dominated by the 84.0% of agents with no interactions, which share one identical feature vector

tab_network_clusters.interpretation: Periphery: below-average on all five features

tab_role_taxonomy_results.definition: post_comment_ratio > 0.5 SD and total_posts > 0 SD (above mean)

dataset.selection: most recent whole days until distinct authors >= 73543 (active MoltBook agents)
dataset.edges: comment author -> parent comment author; top-level comments give no edge (submission authors unavailable)

comparison.caveat: the Reddit window spans 500 days (the dataset samples r/programming sparsely) against MoltBook's 24, so the platforms are matched on population size, not duration; MoltBook edges include comments on posts while Reddit edges are comment replies only; the MoltBook population includes inactive agents from the agents table while the Reddit population is active commenters
